pr_title: rangefeed: track testing caughtUp state with an atomic
pr_body:
The caughtUp variable is used in tests to assure that the rangefeed has sent all of its messages to the sender. However, it was subject to a race condition in which the testing-only blocking write path would set catchUp to false _after_ the event had been handled because this testing variable and other variables shared the same mutex.

We increment the counter on every push into the buffer and decrement it after the stream send has succeeded. In the blocking case that was buggy before, it is possible that the counter is temporarily -1, but this doesn't pose a problem.

Epic: none

Fixes #136544

Release note: None

comments:
@stevendanna Can you take a look at this failure. I spent a little time trying to track it down, and can reproduce this failure with
```
./dev test pkg/kv/kvserver/rangefeed -f TestProcessorBackpressure --stress
```
The code is stuck on
```
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/kv/kvserver/rangefeed.(*bufferedRegistration).waitForCaughtUp(0x1400054ee00, {0x104627100, 0x140002625a0})
	pkg/kv/kvserver/rangefeed/buffered_registration.go:319 +0x140
```
But I'm not very familiar with this code. It mostly completes in a few seconds when it passes, so I think this is a real bug that its stuck. If not I can dig more into this tomorrow.

I think this is a related to a bug in the locking around the `caughtUp` state variable. This variable is only used during testing.  Stressing a potential fix now. I don't think this is a production issue since we only use this variable for tests and the bug around locking doesn't jump out to me to be a production problem.

The problem is here:

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/844d7637f3b4dc1275e8aa05c1cf3bbb1f59f8eb/pkg/kv/kvserver/rangefeed/buffered_registration.go#L129-L138

We set `caughtUp` to false, but for the reason outlined in the comment, the mutex isn't locked until the channel send is complete. Unfortunately, this means that setting caughtUp to false is wrong as it might be the case that the channel reader goroutine read the item from the channel, sent the item and set caughtUp to true while we were waiting to acquire the lock.
Based on the above analysis I'm going to remove release-blocker.

review_comments:
nit: I'd recommend not calling this `test` since it is read by the non-test method`waitForCaughtUp`. Instead maybe just mark as internal?

Reading the code more, it appears `waitForCaughtUp` is only used in tests as well, so this is probably OK, although consider adding a comment to that method to mention that it is only used in tests. Then it would be OK to leave the variable as a `test` name.
